I've been using a fold 4 for past several years as my one and only phone, and its pretty awesome. I mainly use it open because I spend a majority of time reading and browsing the web. I close it to put it in my pocket or when one handed operation is required, and i cant set it down or on something. The screen ratio isn't ideal. I wish the opened screen was less square, more rectangular. To be honest though, I've gotten used to it, since it only really matters for video. Dave is absolutely right that the actual video size is basically the exact same as a bar phone. However, you also get the bottom half to read and type comments while watching a full sized video, or browse. You also get a good picture in picture function. I use these features a lot.

I've found a few uses where dual screen is good to have, like when copying info from one image or app to another, using a calculator or note taking app with web browser (like a recipe, for ingredients or measurements/conversions, which I've used a few times), or using a timer with my workout program on the other side.

The other issue is the durability of the fold area, which has been very questionable for the fold 4. I had a friend with my model who had to get his replaced 3 times. Ive had to replace it once for a different reason. 

Overall, if you put durability aside, its a great phone and i prefer it over regular phones just cause its nice to have so much extra screen real estate for browsing and reading. I use it a ton and almost always in its open state. If you browse the web a ton or a read on your phone a lot, its excellent for that. Im pretty happy with it but not attached to it. I sometimes consider going back but would probably stick with the fold if cost isnt an issue.

comments.text:
Definitely tricky to open. But I worry more about closing, as it requires to push lightly on the screen. However, it means it closes tightly and I'd be very confident that it won't let dirt in. I think it's worth that trade off.

A case will make it easier to open. And eliminate the wobble (otherwise leave it screen down when not in use). 

I thought I would be more flip than fold, but trying out the flip7 I quickly realised I would rarely use it folded. Just too fiddly, apart from the odd widget. So it would be closed only when not in use, and opened up and closed a lot. Which raises durability questions. And the softer screen for daily phone like interacts, felt a step back. I really felt very meh about a product I had seriously been considering.  

The fold7 however, I had rejected for price and YouTubers regularly questioning how useful the tablet mode is. And the opposite happened, I tried it and was floored. I couldn't pick from all the other phones, but this instantly wowed me. Not just the goldilocks between s25+ (good width) and ultra (build, cameras), but attractive especially in blue, no ugly Chinese or Google Cyclops phone module even if the one on board has its own disadvantages. For me, I'm sure I will be 90% phone mode. I have an old 10" tablet I've been thinking about upgrading but didn't as I couldn't justify the cost for an occasional use device. This fixes that problem. I can leave the work iPad at home when travelling. Emails I could always check on my 6' screen, but attachments were annoying, spreadsheets a pain and forget calling someone while viewing docs. 

I get why people that review phones and tech from a tech perspective reject these. If you just view it as a bigger screen for media and games, I think you miss the point and money could be better spent elsewhere. 

For me, as a tool for everyday, family but also work it is convenience and productivity heaven. I really wanted a Microsoft duo when I couldn't afford or justify one. This for me is the evolution of that.

Wow, 9hrs since posting vid and 1,284 comments and counting.  Have not even read them yet though feeling you hit a nerve.  Back in the day I had a fold phone called an Axon M (think it was called).  The 2nd panel was crazy thin, like I figure the Fold 7 though other panel was thicker.  
The unique thing about it was it had coding so that when words spanned the two panels, a character or two would repeat on the 2nd panel such that you could understand the missing letter(s) as you read left panel to right panel.  I wish MS Duo 1 & 2 offered that feature though since it did not you would miss a letter or two as the text flowed from the left to right panel.  A MAJOR fail on MS part I offer.  Though MS did make it a 'book' shape aka a bit wider then other, later to be released fold devices.

Just played a video on the Duo 2 and indeed it does not have massive black bars top and bottom though of course it has that gap between panels which is an issue to watch videos full screen.

I concur about not using multiple floating panels on a fold device.  Have enough issues trying to do it and have all flow nicely on a small MacBook air laptop at times (a windows guy I am mostly).  

Have a Fold 5 and did use the S Pen now and then though not too much.  You make good points concerning the seam in the middle though yes it is something you get used to quickly I feel.  Just hoping the outer screen will be wide enough to live it it for a few years though miss what MS Duo could have been if they had released a Duo 3.

And like you, I mostly just use the larger inside screen for media and news content, not to create content and am ok with that.   The Fold 7 went on a diet and buyers will benefit for it having gone to the gym.
Nice video, thank you
